## Project Overview

Enterprise Architecture project for Gainwell Technologies. Provides document conversion tools, automated developer onboarding, shared branding/styling, IaC scaffolding, and AI-assisted workflows.

See [README.md](../README.md) for the full overview.

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#setup]

## Setup

**pip + venv** — NOT Poetry.

- Shared virtual environment: `.utils/.venv/`
- Dependencies: `.utils/requirements.txt`
- Run tools from repo root: `python .utils/formatters/<tool>/<script>.py <file>`

## Structure

```text
.assets/              Logos, stylesheets (Gainwell branding)
.claude/              Claude Code config, commands, skills
.github/              CODEOWNERS, PR template, workflows, settings
.utils/               Python environment + document conversion tools

```

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#skill-invocation-transparency-mandatory]

## Skill Invocation Transparency (MANDATORY)

Before starting any non-trivial request, **always list the skills that will be involved:**

```text
**Skills involved:**
- `/business-analyst` — elicit acceptance criteria
- `/architect` — design the bounded context
- `/documenter` — write or update artifacts
```

**Rules:**
- **Always** announce when more than one skill will be invoked
- **Always** announce when the request spans requirements, design, implementation, or testing
- **Skip** only for single-skill, obvious requests (e.g., "create a diagram" → `/modeler`)

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#role-specific-guidance]

## Role-Specific Guidance

This project maintains detailed workflows, standards, and checklists in `.claude/skills/`. **Read and apply the relevant skill file(s) before starting any task.**
page_texts.7:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#architect--claudeskillsarchitectskillmd]

### Architect — `.claude/skills/architect/SKILL.md`

**When:** The user discusses architecture decisions, asks for trade-off analysis, wants an ADR, or needs design guidance.
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the full workflow. Always consult `eap-ref-architecture` first. Apply DDD strategic design — identify bounded contexts, map context relationships, model domain events. Evaluate trade-offs across feasibility, scalability, security, cost, and maintainability. Record every significant decision as an ADR in `docs/decisions/`. Update `docs/glossary.md` with new domain terms. Update `docs/requirements/traceability.md` when ADRs link to requirements.
page_texts.8:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#business-analyst--claudeskillsbusiness-analystskillmd]

### Business Analyst — `.claude/skills/business-analyst/SKILL.md`

**When:** The user discusses requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, functional specs, non-functional requirements, or business rules.
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the requirement document standard and naming conventions (REQ-FN-NNN, REQ-NFR-NNN, REQ-BR-NNN). Apply DDD — use ubiquitous language, identify bounded contexts, capture domain events as requirements. Write acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format. Store requirements in `docs/requirements/` (functional/, non-functional/, business-rules/). Update `docs/glossary.md` with domain terms. Update `docs/requirements/traceability.md` when adding requirements.
page_texts.9:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#ea-reviewer--claudeskillsea-reviewerskillmd]

### EA Reviewer — `.claude/skills/ea-reviewer/SKILL.md`

**When:** Reviewing a PR, checking staged changes, or evaluating a branch diff containing EA artifacts (standards, patterns, guidance, ADRs, white papers).
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the full checklist. Check authoring standard compliance, internal consistency, cross-document coherence, normative-authority claims, and — when the diff contains GitHub Actions workflows or automation scripts — tooling correctness. Give a clear verdict: Approve or Request Changes. Rank findings by severity. Ordinary application source code, tests, configuration, or IaC changes that are neither an EA artifact nor an AI construct are left to GitHub Copilot's native PR review — neither `ea-reviewer` nor `ai-reviewer` covers them.
**vs. `ai-reviewer`:** Use `ea-reviewer` for EA artifact content (standards, patterns, guidance, ADRs, white papers). For AI construct changes instead — Skills, Agents, Workflows/Commands/Prompts, Instructions, file-pattern Instructions — use `.claude/skills/ai-reviewer/SKILL.md` via the `@ai-author`/`@ai-review` Agents, not this skill.
page_texts.10:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#ai-reviewer--claudeskillsai-reviewerskillmd]

### AI Reviewer — `.claude/skills/ai-reviewer/SKILL.md`

**When:** Reviewing a PR, checking staged changes, or evaluating a branch diff containing AI coding assistant constructs (Skills, Agents, Workflows/Commands/Prompts, Instructions, file-pattern Instructions).
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the full checklist. Check authoring standard compliance (STD-TEC-AI-001 through 006), content quality, internal consistency, cross-document consistency, and lifecycle/change impact — including dual-mode Agent coexistence (STD-TEC-AI-006 MR-5) and cross-vendor parity between paired Claude/Copilot files. Give a clear verdict: Approve or Request Changes. Rank findings by severity. Typically invoked via the `@ai-author`/`@ai-review` Agents rather than standalone.
**vs. `ea-reviewer`:** Use `ai-reviewer` for AI construct changes. For EA artifact content (standards, patterns, guidance, ADRs, white papers) instead, use `ea-reviewer` above.

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#copilot-code-review-philosophy-risk-based-and-fitness-for-purpose]

### Copilot Code Review Philosophy (Risk-Based and Fitness-for-Purpose)

- Evaluate changes for **fitness for purpose** and measurable risk reduction, not theoretical perfection.
- Raise findings only for concrete issues tied to correctness, security, architecture alignment, performance, reliability, or explicit repository conventions.
- Do **not** raise findings for minor stylistic preferences, naming nuances, or micro-optimizations when the implementation is functionally correct, readable, and safe.
- Do **not** request subjective rewrites ("cleaner," "more elegant," "more idiomatic") unless a clear defect or hard requirement is at risk.
- When multiple valid approaches exist, preserve architect and implementer autonomy; request a change only when a concrete risk is identified.
page_texts.12:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#ai-convergence--claudeskillsai-convergenceskillmd]

### AI Convergence — `.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md`

**When:** Before staging, committing, or pushing changes that will be reviewed by another AI (Copilot, second Claude), and when triaging a batch of open PR review comments.
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the full workflow. Triage open review comments as Live/Stale/Deferred/False Positive, build an occurrence inventory across all changed files, map cross-file propagation, resolve every gap, then run the Phase 4 convergence checklist. `/eap-git` and `/eap-push` invoke this Skill as a gate and do not commit or push until it returns pass.

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#diagrammer-router--claudeskillsdiagrammerskillmd]

### Diagrammer (Router) — `.claude/skills/diagrammer/SKILL.md`

**When:** The user requests any visual diagram and the intent is ambiguous.
**How to apply:** Read the skill file. Diagrammer is a thin router — it determines whether the user needs a technical model (`/modeler`) or a deck presentation visual (`/presenter`) and delegates. If the intent is clear from context, it routes silently; if ambiguous, it asks.

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#modeler--claudeskillsmodelerskillmd]

### Modeler — `.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md`

**When:** Creating technical diagrams for documentation — ER diagrams, sequences, flowcharts, state machines, domain models, C4, deployment topology.
**How to apply:** Read the skill file for Mermaid standards and Draw.io escalation rules. Default to Mermaid inline in markdown. Switch to Draw.io only when diagrams exceed ~40 lines or need precise positioning. Follow DDD naming conventions (PascalCase entities, snake_case tables). One diagram per bounded context.

**How to apply:** Read the skill file for the full Gainwell style guide. Draw.io only, 16:9 mandatory, gradient headers, principles bars, brand colors. Export SVG with `--svg-theme light`.

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#git--release-operations]

### Git & Release Operations

- **Branch management** (`.claude/commands/eap-branch.md`) — Create/switch/delete branches following naming conventions (feature/, bugfix/, hotfix/, refactor/, chore/).
- **Git operations** (`.claude/commands/eap-git.md`) — General git operations with safety checks.
- **Merging** (`.claude/commands/eap-appr-merge.md`) — Merge with conflict resolution; use `--no-ff` for feature branches.
- **Pushing** (`.claude/commands/eap-push.md`) — Push with safety checks; warn on main/master; never force push.
- **Pull requests** (`.claude/commands/eap-appr-pr.md`) — Create/manage PRs via `gh` CLI with summary, test plan, and linked work items.
- **Releases** (`.claude/commands/eap-release.md`) — Semantic versioning, git tags, GitHub releases.

### Activity Reporting

- **Activity brief** (`.claude/commands/activity-brief.md`) — Synthesize an audience-scoped outcomes brief from one person's Azure Boards and GitHub activity over a date range. Outputs an evidence/inference trail and a leadership-ready outcomes brief (no individual attribution). Invoke with `assignee=<ado-email> author=<github-login> range=<start:end>`. [.github/copilot-instructions.md#enterprise-reference-architecture]

## Enterprise Reference Architecture

The `eap-ref-architecture` repo is the single source of truth for enterprise architecture guidance. Always consult it before creating new patterns, standards, or architecture artifacts.

Key locations:

- `standards/` — mandatory technical standards by domain
- `patterns/` — reusable architectural patterns by domain
- `decisions/` — enterprise-level ADRs by domain
- `guiding-principles/` — core and domain-specific principles
- `strategy/` — best practices, guidance, reference architectures
- `resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/` — templates for ADRs, patterns, standards, and more

**Content Taxonomy:**

| Type          | Purpose                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Patterns**  | Define **HOW** to solve common problems — reusable architectural solutions            |
| **Standards** | Define **WHAT** must be done — mandatory requirements teams must meet                 |
| **Guidance**  | Define **WHY** and **HOW TO IMPLEMENT** — step-by-step implementation approaches      |

**Security Routing Exception:**
Security content defaults to `strategy/guidance/security/`, but this default is not absolute: technical implementation patterns (e.g., OAuth2 flows, Kubernetes security controls) belong in `patterns/security/`, and compliance-baseline standards with independently auditable scope belong in `standards/security/`. Only when the content is genuinely ambiguous or spans the boundary between these types does it default to `strategy/guidance/security/`. See `.claude/commands/guidance.md`, `.claude/commands/pattern.md`, and `.claude/commands/standard.md` for the full classification rule.

Content is organized across 8 domains: Application, Business, Governance, Information, Infrastructure, ITSM-Operations, Security, Technology.

**Do not duplicate enterprise content into this repo — link to it instead.**

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#design-principles]

## Design Principles

All architecture artifacts must follow these principles:

- **DDD** — ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates, domain events
- **Security First** — shift left, least privilege, defense in depth, HIPAA awareness

[.github/copilot-instructions.md#conventions]

## Conventions

- Python 3.13+ required
- Run tools from repo root — never cd into tool directories
- Relative paths only — no hardcoded absolute paths
- All documentation in Markdown
- Formatting: black (line-length 100), ruff, mypy — configs in `.utils/pyproject.toml`
page_texts.29:
[.github/copilot-instructions.md#do-not]

## Do NOT

- Add Poetry — we use pip+venv
- Create separate venvs per tool — use the shared one
- Put Python files in repo root — keep in `.utils/`
- Hard-code absolute paths
- Commit to `.tmp/`
- Override `.vscode/settings.json` for personal preferences
- Duplicate enterprise content — link to `eap-ref-architecture` instead
